A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same adaptive principal-eigenvector estimation work. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including v2's new Appendices B and C.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-data simulations comparing adaptive and fully sampled Oja, plus moving-eigenvector tracking experiments in Figures 1 and 2.

after.justification: v2 reports original simulations of convergence, adaptive versus non-adaptive sensing, dimension scaling, tracking and eigengap dependence in Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–4.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same sensing directions, projected Oja update and normalization. However, the corrected S in Theorem 4.1 changes the prescribed warmup duration and constant-then-decaying step sizes relative to v1's Theorem 2, constituting a limited schedule recalibration.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic Gaussian principal-eigenvector estimation with stationary and drifting eigenvectors. The added dimension, eigengap and drift-speed sweeps vary parameters within these retained tasks; no new empirical dataset, domain or distribution family is evaluated.

E2.justification: v1's empirical fully sampled Oja comparator in Figure 1 is removed. v2 instead evaluates non-adaptive random measurements against adaptive sensing in Table 1, with both using two scalar measurements per iteration. This substantially changes the comparative question and comparator set.

E3.justification: The central convergence experiment changes from d=10 to d=64 and uses the revised theorem-based schedule. Added experiments introduce a 0.01/d learning rate, iterations-to-error-0.01 evaluation, dimensions 16–1024 and four eigengap settings. Tracking validation expands to five drift velocities.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct tests of the benefit of adaptivity, dimension-scaling analysis and eigengap sensitivity analysis in Section 6 and Appendix C. The existing tracking analysis gains a multi-velocity comparison of predicted and empirical steady-state errors.

E5.justification: v1 reports averaged convergence trajectories over 20 trials with 20–80 percentile bands. The revised v2 Figure 1 reports medians over 50 trials with 25–75 percentile bands. v2 also introduces least-squares scaling fits; tracking retains 20-trial, 20–80 percentile reporting.

E6.justification: New results include non-adaptive slowdowns of 4.2×, 7.1× and 14× at d=16, 32 and 64 in Table 1, a dimension-scaling exponent of 2.16, and an eigengap-fit slope of −2.42. The original fully sampled comparison is removed and convergence/tracking plots are replaced or expanded. These are changed-setting or newly reported results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds Assouad-based lower bounds for fully observed, adaptive compressed and non-adaptive compressed estimation. The upper-bound proof restores the conditional-covariance contribution, changing S from λ1λ2d²/Δ² + 13λ1d/Δ to 3λ1λ2d²/Δ² + 15λ1d/Δ. Warmup algebra is revised, and Appendix A.2.11 adds an independence/zero-mean condition to the retained tracking derivation.

C1.justification: v1 establishes an upper convergence bound and leaves dimensional optimality open, even suggesting linear dependence might be possible. v2 claims matching minimax optimality at d², a further dimensional penalty for non-adaptive sensing, and a new derivation of the fully observed lower bound. These substantially broaden the principal contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the dimensional penalty as unavoidable and explains adaptivity through signal capture and measurement budgets. It clarifies trailing-eigenspace noise, discusses additive measurement corruption, and replaces generic rank-k future work with specific scaling conjectures and obstacles. Sub-Gaussian extension changes from future work to an asserted extension, while tracking gains an explicit drift assumption.

D1.justification: v2 documents additional parameter grids, target errors and learning rates. Tracking now specifies the rotation rule sin²(θ)=V and initial squared alignment 0.1, improving reproducibility detail beyond v1. Neither version provides implementation code or computing-hardware information.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantive positioning against randomized and batch PCA, citing Halko, Liberty, Musco and Woodruff, and introduces minimax/Assouad references including Vu–Lei, Duchi and van der Vaart. The relationship to prior work shifts from noisy convergence analysis toward optimality and separation of observation regimes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and limitations are extensively rewritten. v2 creates a separate Main Results section, recasts Methods as Proof Techniques, moves the imputation derivation into Appendix A.1, and separates tracking theory from its experimental validation.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column formatting. Both original experimental figures are redesigned, including a joint upper/lower-bound display and multi-panel tracking plots. Dimension and eigengap figures and two numerical tables are added, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects an omitted variance contribution and warmup algebra, states an important tracking assumption, and supplies lower-bound arguments for v1's unresolved optimality question. Direct adaptivity and scaling experiments substantially strengthen the empirical support. These gains outweigh a remaining scope inconsistency: Theorem 4.2 omits the dimension and eigengap restrictions explicitly required in Appendix B.2.6, so its headline optimality claim still needs qualification.
